provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after ut; 1962 sets 'ut, contra'; 1862 sets no comma after omnia; 1962 sets 'omnia, Doctoris'; 1862 capitalises Gentium; 1962 sets gentium lower case; 1862 ornamental initial D is destroyed ('pvKus'), and 'omnia' recognises as '6nuna'; scan artefacts, not readings. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 15075-15079 ('DEus qui cofpicis, quia e[x] nulla noftra actione confidimus: concede propitius: vt contra aduerfa omnia doctoris gentium protectione muniamur. Per Dominum.') -- the 1604 also lacks both commas and sets gentium lower case. 1570 at lines 14552-14556, degraded ('DEug qui cõfpicis q? ex nulla noftra actione confidimus, cocede ppitius: vt cotra aduerfa o[mn]ia, docto?[is] gentiũ protectione munidmur. Per D.'). Corroboration only; the 1570's 'q?' abbreviation could resolve as quia or quod and I do not rest anything on it..
